clue.text: One page in dictionary a student needed about a complex matter

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
one is the Roman numeral I
L is a learner driver's plate, so a student

explanation.surface: A learner looks up a dictionary page to get to grips with a complicated issue.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are given out of order: OED comes first, with I and P following it, then A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Oedipal describes things relating to Freud's Oedipus complex, the psychological complex named after the Greek king.

clue.text: Make one rough, say, knock out another

definitions.text: Make one rough, say, knock out another

parts.words: Make one rough, say, knock out another
parts.note: rough, say, sounds like ruff, the bridge term for playing a trump; here one ruff beats a trump already played by a rival

explanation.surface: Someone roughs up one person so as to knock out a second.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge a ruff is to play a trump card; 'rough, say' points to it by sound. Playing a higher trump than one already on the table beats it.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtrump is to play a higher trump card than an opponent's, beating their ruff in card games like bridge or whist.

clue.text: Relief over the weight chart

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the word for relief is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: relief means aid
a gram is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A relief map is laid over the weight chart.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram is a drawn chart or plan showing how something works or is laid out.

clue.text: Fictitious name gets badly up my nose about Howard's End

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters wrap round the other piece
badly signals that the letters of up my nose are put into a jumbled order
Howard's End means the last letter of the word Howard

explanation.surface: Someone's invented name gets right up a person's nose, with a nod to Forster's novel Howards End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges UP MY NOSE to PSEUONYM, and 'about' puts D, the end of Howard, inside it. The italics suggest Forster's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A pseudonym is an assumed name, such as a pen name used by an author.

clue.text: Old king gets love game

parts.note: Lud was a legendary early king of Britain, remembered in Ludgate
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: An old monarch is given a board game to play.
explanation.walkthrough: King Lud is a legendary ruler of Britain said to have founded London. LUDO is a simple board game played with dice and counters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludo is a children's board game in which counters race round the board on dice throws.

clue.text: Dog rose for walk on Brighton front

indicators.note: in an across clue the walk is placed on, so after, the Brighton letter
front means the first letter of the word Brighton

parts.note: to ramble is to walk for pleasure in the country

explanation.surface: A dog walker heads for a stroll on the Brighton seafront.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton is an English seaside town; its 'front' suggests the promenade, but here it is just the first letter, B.
explanation.definitionFit: Bramble is used loosely for the thorny dog rose as well as the blackberry, both prickly wild shrubs of hedgerows.

clue.text: Indicating person about to give an address

definitions.meaning: to bespeak something is to indicate or suggest it

definitions.text: person about to give an address
definitions.meaning: someone due to make a speech will soon be talking to the audience

explanation.definitionFit: To bespeak is to show or suggest; read as two words, a speaker-to-be will soon be talking.

clue.text: Sharp edge to a couple of notes

parts.note: re and te are two notes of the sol-fa scale
te is another note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A tune gets a sharp edge from two particular notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharp' looks musical beside 'notes', but it describes a ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: An arete is a narrow, knife-like mountain ridge carved by glaciers.

clue.text: Subaltern, upset, concealed nothing the code of chivalry required

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the abbreviation is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: sub is a short form of subaltern, a junior army officer
concealed means hid
nothing is zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: An upset junior officer kept quiet about nothing, as his chivalrous code demanded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required' just closes the surface; a subaltern is a junior officer in the British army.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushido is the samurai's code of honour in feudal Japan, stressing loyalty and courage.

clue.text: See about a right forward

indicators.note: about means the bishop's seat goes round the other letters

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in England

explanation.surface: A coach tells someone to look at a right forward on the team.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'see' is a bishop's diocese; ELY, a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, is the crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward can mean ahead of time or precocious, so a forward child is advanced, developing sooner than usual.

clue.text: Escape the clutches of boy rejected by sweetheart

indicators.note: rejected signals that the boy's name is sent back, read backwards

parts.note: Dave is a boy's name
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: A lad dumped by his girlfriend wriggles free of her grip.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to avoid or slip away from capture, getting out of someone's grasp.

clue.text: Where the pharmacist draws his money?

definitions.text: Where the pharmacist draws his money?

parts.words: Where the pharmacist draws his money?
parts.note: a pharmacist is one who makes up medicines, and the machine giving out cash shares that title

explanation.definitionFit: A dispenser is a chemist making up prescriptions, and a cash machine is also called a cash dispenser.

clue.text: Philippic from one caught in traffic

indicators.note: caught in means the numeral is held inside the word for business

parts.note: traffic as a noun or verb means trade or dealing
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A driver stuck in a jam launches into a rant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traffic' suggests cars, but it means dealing, TRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A philippic is a bitter denunciation, named after Demosthenes' speeches against Philip of Macedon; a long angry speech.

clue.text: Big name bowled out by speed

indicators.note: out means the cricket letter is removed from the famous person

parts.note: a big name is a celebrity, a famous person
B is the cricket abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A star batsman is bowled out by a fast delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket scorecards, b stands for bowled; removing it from CELEBRITY leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Celerity is a formal word for swiftness or rapidity of movement.

clue.text: Damage tomb occupied by popular German nobleman

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil

indicators.note: occupied by means the burial place has the other word placed within it

parts.note: a grave is a tomb
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A popular German aristocrat's tomb is vandalised.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: strictly the wife of a margrave, a German noble title.
explanation.definitionFit: A margravine is the wife of a margrave, a German marquis or border lord, so the noble household's lady rather than the man.

clue.text: Demoralise a French soldier

parts.note: un is French for a
man means a soldier, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Someone tries to break the spirit of a French soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: To unman someone is to deprive them of courage or self-control, sapping their nerve.

clue.text: Part of joint bank, perhaps, one involving the French

indicators.note: involving means the rearranged letters and the next word take in the French article
perhaps hints that the letters of the word bank could be arranged another way

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: A joint bank account perhaps includes one for a French partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' makes ANKB, and 'involving' sets the French article inside it. The phrase 'joint bank' suggests a shared account, but the joint is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle bone, or talus, forms the lower part of the ankle joint.

clue.text: Enough space here for Katisha's exhibition?

definitions.meaning: Katisha in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado boasts of her right elbow, which people come miles to see

explanation.definitionFit: Elbow room is ample space to move; a room to show off Katisha's famous elbow would be one too.

clue.text: Oriental novelist occupying attention

indicators.note: occupying means the writer sits inside the word for attention

parts.note: ear means attention, as in lend an ear
Laurence Sterne was the novelist who wrote Tristram Shandy

explanation.surface: A novelist from the Orient grabs everyone's attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental means from the East, so a native of Asia is an inhabitant of eastern lands.

clue.text: Grouse, though initially silent

parts.note: names a game bird of the grouse family whose spelling begins with a letter that is not pronounced

explanation.definitionFit: The ptarmigan is a mountain grouse, and its P is silent in speech.

clue.text: Crook is saved by counsels

indicators.note: crook as an adjective means bent or twisted, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A criminal is let off by his lawyers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' reads as a criminal noun, but it signals that IS SAVED is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To counsel someone is to give them advice, so counsels is a synonym for gives guidance.

clue.text: Champions among the three-quarters

definitions.meaning: to champion a cause is to support it, as a verb
in rugby the three-quarters are the players who line up behind the forwards

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who supports a cause stands behind it; in rugby the three-quarters belong to the back line.

clue.text: Clot justifies unceremonious dismissal most of all

parts.note: conge is an abrupt dismissal, from French

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the word all is cut off

explanation.surface: A fool defends the sacking most of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clot' is a verb here; 'justifies' is a joining word. CONGE (often with an accent) is a curt farewell or sacking.
explanation.definitionFit: To congeal is to thicken and set, as blood or fat does on cooling.

clue.text: Short stories featuring the new girl's return

parts.note: novel means new or original

indicators.note: return signals that the girl's name is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally

explanation.surface: Short stories star a new girl coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' seems to describe the girl, but it is its own piece, NOVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A novella is a work of fiction longer than a short story but shorter than a novel.

clue.text: Part of marina dirty at deepest point

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A section of the harbour is filthy, at its lowest ebb.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of anything, the opposite of the zenith.

clue.text: Base notes expressing mood, say

parts.note: base means low, as in base instincts
E is a musical note
D is another musical note

explanation.surface: Low notes in music express a particular mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mood, say' sounds like 'mooed', what cattle did, which is the meaning of the answer. 'expressing' joins the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle that lowed made their deep call, which sounds the same as 'mooed', a near-twin of the clue word.

clue.text: Twitch string holding key

indicators.note: holding means the cord wraps round the musical letter

parts.note: twine is strong string
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: A string twitches when tied round a key.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinge is a sudden sharp pain or pang, a nervous twitch of feeling.

clue.text: Keen to move sweet little Miss Brown up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the whole run is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to go is to move
the song Sweet Georgia Brown supplies Georgia, and little Georgia is its abbreviation GA

explanation.surface: Someone is eager to move a sweet little girl upstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses GO and GA together. 'Sweet Georgia Brown' is a jazz standard; GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means eager and excited, waiting with great interest.

clue.text: Refusing to recognise the college one's entered

indicators.note: entered means the short piece is put into the college's name

parts.note: Downing is a college of Cambridge University
one's read as one is gives I and IS, I standing for one

explanation.surface: A college refuses to acknowledge one of its own entrants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is', so I + S = IS.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown someone is to reject or repudiate them, denying any connection.

clue.text: A great expanse, once a shambles

indicators.note: a shambles is a complete mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A vast area that was once in chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean is a vast body of salt water covering much of the globe.

clue.text: Exceptional rise expected from the surplus

indicators.note: exceptional suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters are put out of their usual order

parts.note: due means expected, as in the train is due

explanation.surface: An unusual rise is forecast from the surplus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exceptional' rearranges RISE with DUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what is left over, the remainder or excess.

clue.text: Skipper, say, is the one who takes risks

indicators.note: say signals that a word is to be taken by how it is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a skipper is one who skips or frisks about, a gamboller

explanation.surface: A boat's captain is the one in the crew who takes chances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skipper' suggests a captain, but here it is one who skips, a gamboller, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambler is a person who bets or takes chances with money or fate.
